title: Per-event coverage report
description: One row of data/curated/event-coverage.jsonl for every selected event: the aggregation of its games' per-game coverage markers (spec R6) into the three field groups the markers name. `coverage.<group>` counts the event's games by marker, so `complete` is a number of games and not a claim about the event; `state` is the worst case over those games — `complete` only when every game is, `unavailable` when none has anything in the group or the event carries no games at all, `partial` otherwise. The build generates this file from the emitted games, and the invariant gate re-counts it against games.jsonl, so an event can never be reported more complete than its games: that is ticket 10's reconciliation criterion. `eras` lists the era-table windows the event's games fall in, so a game-level report can be joined to the era-level one; it is empty exactly when `games` is 0. `games` reconciles with event-games.jsonl and with the rows of games.jsonl.

eventName.description: The event's display name, repeated so the row reads without a join (spec R12).

overviewPage.description: The event's source page, so a reader can find the payload that answered for it.

eras.description: The distinct era ids among this event's games, sorted; empty when the event carries no games (an `empty` or `missing` event, per event-games.jsonl).

games.description: How many rows this event contributes to games.jsonl, which is also the number of games each group's counts sum to.

coverage.description: The three field groups a game's coverage marker names, aggregated over this event's games. Keys are the ones games.jsonl uses.

state.description: The group's state over the whole event: `complete` only when every game is, `unavailable` when none carries anything or there are no games, `partial` otherwise.
